On Tue, May 14, 2029 at 08:22, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Immediate plan:

I've pulled a 30-minute trace window (02:00–02:30 PT) and attached the snapshot (trace_snapshot_20290514.tar.gz). Quick notes from initial triage:

- We see queue depth spikes on the us-west serving cluster for the model variant OP-standard-v2 at 02:05 and again at 02:17. The Q depth reaches ~350 (baseline ~80 for that pool).
- Concurrency cap enforcement on that pool kicked in and caused soft-evictions; many requests were requeued to the overflow tier which has higher p95.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped for certain conversation prefixes used by OrbitPay's routing rules — likely due to a burst of long-context requests from a merchant that uses longer prompts.
- Error rate did not significantly increase (5xxs stayed low) — this looks like latency/backpressure rather than a crash.

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
1) Temporarily increase the dedicated pool size for OP-standard-v2 by adding two additional nodes (30 min to warm).
2) Relax concurrency cap by +15% for OrbitPay routes to avoid thrashing into overflow.
3) Backfill prefix cache for merchant-heavy prefixes and enable conservative batching for those routes.

I'll stand by to apply the changes once we have OrbitPay sign-off on a temporary capacity bump.

—Dev
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Folks — applying mitigations now per OrbitPay approval. Quick notes for exec summary (draft):

Timeline (draft):
- 02:00 PT — OrbitPay dashboards begin showing p95/p99 drift.
- 02:05/PT — queue depth spike observed on us-west serving cluster for OP-standard-v2 (Q ~350).
- 02:07/PT — concurrency cap enforcement caused requeueing to overflow pool; p99 rose further.
- 02:17/PT — second burst correlating with merchant m-8363 long-context requests; KV cache hit-rate dropped for that prefix.
- 02:26/PT — mitigations initiated (capacity bump + relax cap + prefix backfill); p95 trending back to baseline by ~02:50.

Proposed medium-term fixes:
- Route-level bounded context enforcement (reject or truncate excessively long contexts at ingress with 429 + guidance) — avoids KV churn.
- Adaptive concurrency caps: auto-relax short-term when overflow is increasing instead of hard evictions.
- Heat-mapping for prefix cache: proactively prewarm cache for merchant/route combos with repeated long contexts.
- Capacity smoothing: improve autoscaler thresholds to avoid undershoot on sudden persistent bursts.

Marissa/Karthik/Dylan — can you validate ETA/effort estimates for the fix list so we can include them in the exec note to OrbitPay? I will send the exec summary once I have numbers.

—Tessa
